key_insight: DEFEAT makes crystal composition and occupancy differentiable, enabling joint gradient-based optimization of elements, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables targeted searches for superconductors and photovoltaic absorbers while incorporating predicted properties and an energy penalty.
method: Extend pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Combine fine-tuned property-model gradients with a machine-learned energy penalty to optimize crystals.
Evaluate designs using first-principles calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition with machine-learned potentials.
evidence_signal: DFPT evaluation found Allen–Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39 of 45 structurally novel designs, peaking at 24.0 K; SCAN confirmed ten novel absorber structures within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on raw or corrected gap scales and within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias can propagate into designs unless corrected in the objective, and finite-temperature phase competition can reorder static-hull rankings.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
